$comment: What this repo can deploy. One entry per AppSail; `node scripts/deploy.mjs <target>
<service>` reads this alongside deploy/targets.json.
The two files answer different questions. targets.json says WHERE a deploy lands —
which Zoho account, project and environment. This one says WHAT is deployed:
source        the folder uploaded as the AppSail. `build_path` is `.` relative to
it, so EVERYTHING in this folder is zipped — which is exactly why
`localEnv` below has to be parked out of the way during upload.
appsail       default AppSail name. A target may override it — see below.
appConfigBase committed template. No secrets.
appConfigOut  generated per deploy from the target's envFile. Gitignored, because
its env_variables carry real secrets.
localEnv      the developer's own .env inside `source`.
build         root package.json script names, run in order. A service with no
frontend simply lists fewer.
requiredEnv   keys whose absence makes the deployed app refuse to boot. Checked
before anything is built or uploaded — otherwise the failure surfaces
at the next cold start instead of at deploy time.
catalyst.json is GENERATED from this file at deploy time, holding only the one service
being deployed. That is what makes `catalyst deploy --only appsail` push one AppSail
rather than every entry. It is gitignored; do not commit it.
Per-target names: `appsail` here is the default, and a target's services block may
override it. That is how one service can be a genuinely different AppSail in each Zoho
account — which the accounts service needs, since staging and production are separate
accounts in separate data centres. This is only safe because catalyst.json is
generated; while it was committed, one name had to serve both projects (guide §1.5).
Adding a service: add an entry here, give every target in targets.json its own
services.<name>.envFile, and add its npm scripts to the root package.json.
🔴 `accounts` is wired end to end — accounts/, its app-config.base.json, the
build:accounts script and `npm run deploy:<target>:accounts` all exist — but it has
NEVER BEEN DEPLOYED, and two things are still missing. (1) Neither .env.<target>
file exists: only accounts/.env.production.example is committed, so a deploy stops
at the env-file check before it builds or uploads anything. (2) The AppSail itself
must already exist in the target's Catalyst project — production has no `appsail`
override, so the name is `octfis-accounts`; if that AppSail is absent the CLI drops
into its interactive create flow mid-deploy. Its `requiredEnv` is the minimum the
design fixes (docs/SSO_AND_IDENTITY.md §14: DATABASE_URL because all state lives in
our Postgres, OIDC_ISSUER because the issuer is baked into every token and cannot
change later). Signing keys are NOT here — §7.3 keeps them in the signing_keys
table, not an env var. Grow the list as the service grows.
